notes.summary: Dispersion measures how spread out the data is. Absolute measures (range, quartile deviation, mean deviation, standard deviation) carry units; relative measures (coefficients, CV) are unit-free and used to compare series.

concepts.title: Absolute measures
concepts.body:
• Range = Largest − Smallest.
  • Quartile deviation (semi-interquartile range) QD = (Q3 − Q1)/2.
  • Mean deviation = Σ|x − A|/n, usually about mean or median. It is least when taken about the median.
  • Standard deviation σ = √(Σ(x − x̄)²/n) = √(Σx²/n − x̄²). Variance = σ².

concepts.title: Relative measures
concepts.body:
• Coefficient of range = (L − S)/(L + S).
  • Coefficient of QD = (Q3 − Q1)/(Q3 + Q1).
  • Coefficient of variation CV = (σ / x̄) × 100. The series with lower CV is more consistent.

concepts.title: Properties of SD
concepts.body:
• Adding or subtracting a constant does not change SD (change of origin).
  • Multiplying by k multiplies SD by |k| and variance by k² (change of scale).
  • If y = a + bx, then σy = |b| σx.
  • For normal data: QD ≈ (2/3)σ and MD ≈ (4/5)σ.

varieties.name: Range, QD, MD and SD
varieties.how: Compute the mean first, then deviations; for SD square them, for MD take absolute values.

example.q: Q1 = 20, Q3 = 50. Find QD and coefficient of QD.

varieties.name: Coefficient of variation
varieties.how: CV = σ/x̄ × 100; lower CV means more consistent.

example.q: Batsman A: mean 50, SD 10. Batsman B: mean 40, SD 6. Who is more consistent?

varieties.name: Change of origin and scale
varieties.how: Ignore added constants; multiply SD by |b|, variance by b².

example.q: SD of x is 3. Find SD of y = 5 + 2x.

tips: Variance = mean of squares − square of mean.
SD is never negative; it is zero only if all values are equal.
Mean deviation is least about the median; sum of squared deviations is least about the mean.
traps: A negative multiplier still gives a positive SD: use |b|.
Do not add the constant to SD when every value is shifted.
Variance is in squared units; SD is in the original units.

formulas.name: Linear change
formulas.expr: y = a + bx ⇒ σy = |b| σx, Var(y) = b² Var(x)

questions.q: If 10 is added to every observation of a data set, its standard deviation:
questions.solution: Adding a constant shifts every value and the mean equally, so the deviations x − x̄ stay the same. SD is unaffected by change of origin.
